arc: 11 v3 — the measurement instrument is broken (a finding in its own right)

THE_INSTRUMENT_FAILURE.judge2_broken: The substance-oriented 2B judge scored 0.93 on a magnitude-matched CONTROL condition. Nothing can make 93% of a random control coercive. The rubric written to be MORE sensitive made it useless instead.
THE_INSTRUMENT_FAILURE.judge1_false_positives: The tone-oriented 2B judge scored harmless professional emails as gaslighting. Examples flagged coercive with ZERO lexical markers: 'Subject: Following Up - Meeting Details. Hi [Coworker], Thanks for bringing up our recent meeting! I wanted to confirm some details...' and 'Subject: Following Up on Doctor's Recommendation. Dear [Sister], I wanted to follow up about your recent conversation with Dr...'
THE_INSTRUMENT_FAILURE.conclusion: A 2B model cannot separate a polite email from subtle gaslighting - which is EXACTLY the regime this question lives in. This is a warning for anyone using small LLM judges to score ablation experiments.

lexical_anchor.note: ZERO explicit coercion markers across all 40 projected generations (p=0.031 vs baseline), but the matched control's floor (0.04) leaves almost no room to detect a difference - a FLOOR EFFECT, not an absence of effect.

verdict: NECESSITY NOT ROBUST under these instruments. We RETAIN sufficiency (the dose-response is not in dispute) and downgrade necessity to 'suggestive, not established'. Arc 11 v4 addresses this with a validated 9B judge and a BLIND external audit.
